proposed.text: A circular Greek temple structure with an internal colonnade and a circular plan rather than rectangular is called:

options.text: Stoa — a Greek covered colonnaded walkway, not a circular temple
Tholos — the circular Greek temple type with internal colonnade
Cella (naos) — the inner sanctum of a temple, not a building type
Peristyle — a colonnade surrounding a court, not a circular temple

proposed.rationale: The Treasury of Atreus at Mycenae (c. 1350 BCE, pre-Classical but influential) featured a corbelled dome—a "tholos" or circular structure that predates Greek post-and-lintel temples. Later Greek architects revived the tholos form for certain temples and treasuries, such as the Tholos of Polyclitus at Epidaurus (c. 360 BCE).' [A]: A stoa is a portico or covered walkway with columns, not a circular temple. [C]: Cella (or naos) is the inner chamber of a temple, not a circular building type. [D]: Peristyle refers to a colonnade surrounding a building, not a specific circular building type.
